title_en: Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 Persistent and frequent domestic violence may be determined as "maltreatment" as referred to in Articles 1042, 1079, and 1091 of the Civil Code.

Article 2 The circumstance of "cohabitation with another person" as prescribed in Articles 1042, 1079, and 1091 of the Civil Code means a person with a spouse continuously and stably cohabits with a person of the opposite sex other than his or her spouse without using the title of husband and wife.

Article 3 Where a party institutes a lawsuit merely requesting the dissolution of a cohabitation relationship, the People's Court shall not accept the case; if the case has already been accepted, the People's Court shall render a ruling to dismiss the action.
Where a party institutes a lawsuit due to a dispute over property division or child support during the period of cohabitation, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 4 Where a party institutes a lawsuit based solely on Article 1043 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall not accept the case; if the case has already been accepted, the People's Court shall render a ruling to dismiss the action.

Article 5 Where a party requests the return of betrothal gifts given in accordance with customs, if it is determined that the following circumstances are present, the People's Court shall support the request:
(1) The parties have not gone through the marriage registration procedures;
(2) The parties have gone through the marriage registration procedures but have not actually lived together; or
(3) The gifts were given before marriage and have caused the giver to suffer financial hardship.
The application of the provisions in items (2) and (3) of the preceding paragraph shall be subject to the condition that the parties have divorced.
II. Marriage

Article 6 Where a man and a woman retroactively undergo marriage registration in accordance with the provisions of Article 1049 of the Civil Code, the validity of the marital relationship shall be calculated from the time when both parties meet the substantive requirements for marriage as prescribed by the Civil Code.

Article 7 Where a man and a woman who have not undergone marriage registration in accordance with the provisions of Article 1049 of the Civil Code but have lived together under the title of husband and wife institute a lawsuit for divorce, the case shall be dealt with differently:
(1) If, before the date of February 1, 1994, when the Ministry of Civil Affairs promulgated and implemented the Regulations on Marriage Registration Administration, both parties had already met the substantive requirements for marriage, the case shall be dealt with as a de facto marriage.
(2) If, on or after the date of February 1, 1994, when the Ministry of Civil Affairs promulgated and implemented the Regulations on Marriage Registration Administration, both parties meet the substantive requirements for marriage, the People's Court shall inform them to retroactively undergo marriage registration. If they fail to do so, the case shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 3 of this Interpretation.

Article 8 Where a man and a woman who have not undergone marriage registration in accordance with the provisions of Article 1049 of the Civil Code but have lived together under the title of husband and wife, and one party dies, the other party claiming inheritance rights in the capacity of a spouse shall be dealt with in accordance with the principles of Article 7 of this Interpretation.

Article 9 The subjects who have the right to request the People's Court to confirm the invalidity of a marriage that has already undergone marriage registration in accordance with the provisions of Article 1051 of the Civil Code include the parties to the marriage and interested persons. Among them, interested persons include:
(1) In the case where the ground is bigamy, the close relatives of the parties and the basic-level organization;
(2) In the case where the ground is failing to reach the legal age for marriage, the close relatives of the person who has not reached the legal age for marriage; and
(3) In the case where the ground is the existence of a prohibited kinship relationship for marriage, the close relatives of the parties.

Article 10 Where a party requests the People's Court to confirm the invalidity of a marriage in accordance with the provisions of Article 1051 of the Civil Code, if the statutory circumstance for an invalid marriage has already ceased to exist at the time the lawsuit is instituted, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Article 11 After the People's Court accepts a case requesting confirmation of the invalidity of a marriage, if the plaintiff applies to withdraw the action, it shall not be permitted.
Mediation shall not apply to the trial of the validity of the marriage; a judgment shall be made in accordance with law.
If the case involves property division and child support, mediation may be conducted. If a mediation agreement is reached, a separate mediation document shall be prepared; if no mediation agreement is reached, a judgment covering all issues shall be rendered.

Article 12 After the People's Court accepts a divorce case, if it is determined through trial that the marriage is indeed invalid, the People's Court shall inform the parties of the circumstance of the invalidity and render a judgment confirming the invalidity of the marriage in accordance with law.

Article 13 Where the People's Court has separately accepted a case involving a divorce and a case requesting confirmation of the invalidity of a marriage with respect to the same marital relationship, the trial of the divorce case shall be conducted after a judgment is rendered in the case requesting confirmation of the invalidity of the marriage.

Article 14 After one or both spouses die, if the surviving spouse or an interested person requests confirmation of the invalidity of the marriage in accordance with the provisions of Article 1051 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 15 Where an interested person requests the People's Court to confirm the invalidity of a marriage in accordance with the provisions of Article 1051 of the Civil Code, the interested person shall be the plaintiff, and both parties to the marital relationship shall be the defendants.
If one spouse has died, the surviving spouse shall be the defendant.

Article 16 When the People's Court tries a case involving an invalid marriage caused by bigamy, if the case involves property disposition, the legitimate spouse of the marriage shall be permitted to participate in the proceedings as a third party with independent claims.

Article 17 Where a party requests confirmation of the invalidity of a marriage on grounds other than the three types of invalid marriages prescribed in Article 1051 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall render a judgment to dismiss the party's claim.
Where a party institutes a civil action on the grounds of a defect in the marriage registration procedure, claiming to revoke the marriage registration, the party shall be informed that he or she may apply for administrative reconsideration or institute an administrative action in accordance with law.

Article 18 Where an actor, by threatening to cause harm to the life, body, health, reputation, or property of the other party or his or her close relatives, compels the other party to enter into a marriage against his or her true will, this may be determined as "duress" as referred to in Article 1052 of the Civil Code.
Where a request to revoke the marriage is made on the ground of duress, only the party to the marital relationship who was subjected to the duress may make such a request.

Article 19 The "one year" prescribed in Article 1052 of the Civil Code shall not be subject to the provisions on suspension, interruption, or extension of the statute of limitations.
Where a party who has been subjected to duress or has been unlawfully restricted of personal freedom requests the revocation of the marriage, the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 152 of the Civil Code shall not apply.

Article 20 The phrase "shall have no legal binding force from the very beginning" as prescribed in Article 1054 of the Civil Code means that an invalid marriage or a voidable marriage shall be determined to be not protected by law from the very beginning only when it is confirmed as invalid or revoked in accordance with law.

Article 21 Where a People's Court confirms the invalidity of a marriage or revokes a marriage upon the request of a party according to law, it shall confiscate the marriage certificates of both parties and send the effective judgment to the local marriage registration authority.

Article 22 For a marriage confirmed invalid or revoked, the property acquired by the parties during their cohabitation shall be treated as jointly owned, unless there is evidence proving that it is owned by one of the parties alone.
III. Marital Relationship

Article 23 Where a husband claims damages on the grounds that the wife's unauthorized termination of pregnancy infringes upon his right to reproduction, the People's Court shall not support such claim. Where a dispute arises between the husband and wife over whether to have children, leading to the complete breakdown of their relationship, and one party requests a divorce, the People's Court, if mediation fails, shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 1079, Paragraph 3, Item 5 of the Civil Code.

Article 24 The "income from intellectual property rights" as provided in Article 1062, Paragraph 1, Item 3 of the Civil Code refers to the property income actually obtained or clearly obtainable during the existence of the marital relationship.
Article 26 Income generated after marriage from the personal property of one spouse, except for natural fruits and natural appreciation, shall be recognized as marital joint property.

Article 27 A house leased by one party before marriage and purchased with joint property after marriage, which is registered under the name of one party, shall be recognized as marital joint property.

Article 28 Where one party sells a house jointly owned by the spouses without the consent of the other party, and a third party purchases it in good faith, pays a reasonable price, and has completed the real estate registration, the People's Court shall not support the other party's claim to recover the house.
Where one spouse's unauthorized disposal of jointly owned property causes loss to the other spouse, and, upon divorce, the other spouse requests compensation for the loss, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 29 Where, before the parties marry, the parents contribute funds for the purchase of a house for both parties, such contribution shall be recognized as a gift to their own child individually, unless the parents explicitly indicate that it is a gift to both parties.
Where, after the parties marry, the parents contribute funds for the purchase of a house for both parties, the matter shall be handled according to any agreement; in the absence of an agreement or where the agreement is unclear, it shall be handled in accordance with the principle provided in Article 1062, Paragraph 1, Item 4 of the Civil Code.
Article 30 A soldier's casualty insurance benefits, disability subsidies, and medical and living allowances shall be personal property.

Article 31 Personal property of one spouse as provided in Article 1063 of the Civil Code shall not be converted into marital joint property due to the continuation of the marital relationship, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.

Article 32 Where, before marriage or during the existence of the marital relationship, the parties agree that one party will donate a house owned by that party to the other party or for joint ownership, and the donor revokes the donation before the registration of the transfer of ownership of the donated house, and the other party requests a court order for continued performance, the People's Court may handle the matter in accordance with Article 658 of the Civil Code.

Article 33 Where a creditor asserts a claim against the spouse of a debtor regarding a personal debt incurred by one party before marriage, the People's Court shall not support such claim, unless the creditor can prove that the debt was used for the common living of the family after marriage.

Article 34 Where one spouse colludes with a third party to fabricate a debt, and the third party claims that such debt is a marital joint debt, the People's Court shall not support such claim.
Where one spouse incurs a debt in engaging in illegal or criminal activities such as gambling or drug abuse, and a third party claims that such debt is a marital joint debt, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Article 35 Where the parties' divorce agreement or an effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document of the People's Court has already dealt with the division of marital property, creditors shall still have the right to assert their claims regarding marital joint debts against the man and the woman.
Where one party has borne the liability for satisfying marital joint debts, and claims that the other party shall assume the corresponding debts in accordance with the divorce agreement or the legal documents of the People's Court, the People's Court shall support such claim.
Article 36 Where one spouse dies, the surviving spouse shall bear the liability for satisfying the marital joint debts incurred during the existence of the marital relationship.

Article 37 With respect to the phrase "the counterparty knows of such agreement" as mentioned in Article 1065, Paragraph 3 of the Civil Code, the spouse concerned shall bear the burden of adducing evidence.

Article 38 During the existence of the marital relationship, except for the circumstances provided in Article 1066 of the Civil Code, where one spouse requests a division of the joint property, the People's Court shall not support such request.
IV. Parent-Child Relationship

Article 39 Where a father or mother files a lawsuit with the People's Court requesting the denial of a parent-child relationship, and has provided necessary evidence to prove such claim, and the other party has no contrary evidence and refuses to undergo a paternity test, the People's Court may find that the claim of the party denying the parent-child relationship is established.
Where a father or mother, as well as an adult child, files a lawsuit requesting the confirmation of a parent-child relationship, and provides necessary evidence to prove such claim, and the other party has no contrary evidence and refuses to undergo a paternity test, the People's Court may find that the claim of the party seeking confirmation of the parent-child relationship is established.

Article 40 Where, during the existence of the marital relationship, both spouses unanimously consent to artificial insemination, the child born shall be deemed a legitimate child, and the relevant provisions of the Civil Code shall apply to the relationship of rights and obligations between the parents and the child.

Article 41 An adult child who is still receiving education at or below the senior high school level, or who is unable to maintain a normal livelihood due to non-subjective reasons such as total or partial loss of the ability to work, may be determined as an 'adult child incapable of independent living' as provided in Article 1067 of the Civil Code.
Article 42 The term 'child support' as used in Article 1067 of the Civil Code includes expenses for the child's living expenses, education fees, medical expenses, and similar costs.

Article 43 Where, during the subsistence of a marital relationship, both or one of the parents refuse to perform the obligation of raising a child, and a minor child or an adult child incapable of independent living requests the payment of child support, the People's Court shall support such a request.

Article 45 Where both parents agree that the father shall directly raise the child under the age of two, and such an arrangement has no adverse effect on the healthy growth of the child, the People's Court shall support such an agreement.

Article 47 Where the conditions of both parents for raising the child are substantially similar, and both request direct custody, but the child has lived alone with the paternal or maternal grandparents for many years, and the grandparents request and have the ability to help take care of the grandchild, this may be considered as a priority condition for the father or mother to directly raise the child.

Article 48 On the premise that it is conducive to protecting the interests of the child, where both parents agree to take turns directly raising the child, the People's Court shall support such an agreement.

Article 49 The amount of child support may be determined based on the actual needs of the child, the financial capacity of both parents, and the local actual standard of living.
For a parent with a fixed income, child support shall generally be paid at a rate of twenty to thirty percent of the monthly total income. Where the parent bears child support for two or more children, the percentage may be appropriately increased, but shall generally not exceed fifty percent of the monthly total income.
For a parent without a fixed income, the amount of child support may be determined based on the total annual income or the average income in the same industry, with reference to the above percentages.
Under special circumstances, the above percentages may be appropriately increased or decreased.
Article 50 Child support shall be paid periodically, and may be paid in a lump sum where conditions permit.
Article 51 Where one parent has no economic income or is missing, their property may be used to offset child support.

Article 52 Both parents may agree that one party shall directly raise the child and bear all child support. However, if the direct custodian's raising capacity is clearly insufficient to cover the child's necessary expenses, thereby affecting the child's healthy growth, the People's Court shall not support such an agreement.

Article 53 The period for the payment of child support shall generally last until the child reaches the age of eighteen.
Where a child aged sixteen or older but under eighteen relies mainly on their labor income as a source of livelihood and can maintain the local general standard of living, the parents may cease paying child support.

Article 54 Where the biological father divorces the stepmother, or the biological mother divorces the stepfather, and the stepfather or stepmother does not agree to continue raising the stepchild who was once raised and educated by them, the child shall still be raised by the biological father or biological mother.
Article 55 After divorce, where one parent requests a change in the custody arrangement, or the child requests an increase in child support, a separate action shall be filed.
Article 57 Where both parents agree to change the child custody arrangement, the People's Court shall support such an agreement.

Article 59 Parents may not refuse to pay child support because the child changes their surname. Where a dispute arises due to one parent arbitrarily changing the child's surname to that of the stepmother or stepfather, the original surname shall be restored by order.
Article 60 During the period of a divorce action, where both parties refuse to raise the child, it may be preliminarily ruled that one party shall temporarily raise the child.

Article 81 During the existence of a marital relationship, where one spouse, as an heir, has an estate that may be inherited according to law but has not yet been actually divided among the heirs, and the other spouse requests division at the time of filing for divorce, the People's Court shall inform the parties to file a separate lawsuit after the estate is actually divided among the heirs.

Article 82 Where a loan agreement is concluded between spouses, under which community property is lent to one spouse for personal business operations or other personal affairs, it shall be deemed as an act of the parties agreeing to dispose of community property, and at the time of divorce, it may be handled in accordance with the provisions of the loan agreement.

Article 83 After divorce, where one party files a lawsuit with the People's Court requesting division on the ground that there remains community property not yet disposed of, if upon examination the property is indeed community property not involved at the time of divorce, the People's Court shall divide it according to law.

Article 84 The statute of limitations for a party to file a lawsuit with the People's Court under Article 1,092 of the Civil Code, requesting a second division of community property, shall be three years, commencing from the date the party discovers the relevant facts.

Article 85 Where one spouse applies for preservation measures against the other spouse's separate property or community property, the People's Court may, within the scope of potential losses from such preservation measures, determine a reasonable amount of property security based on the actual circumstances.

Article 86 The 'damages' provided for in Article 1,091 of the Civil Code include both material damages and moral damages. Where moral damages are involved, the relevant provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Moral Damages in Civil Torts shall apply.

Article 87 The subject liable for damages under Article 1,091 of the Civil Code shall be the spouse of the innocent party in the divorce proceedings.
In cases where the People's Court decides against granting the divorce, any request for damages by a party based on Article 1,091 of the Civil Code shall not be upheld.
During the existence of the marital relationship, if a party files a claim for damages solely under Article 1,091 of the Civil Code without filing for divorce, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

Article 88 When accepting a divorce case, the People's Court shall inform the parties in writing of their relevant rights and obligations under Article 1,091 of the Civil Code and other provisions. In applying Article 1,091 of the Civil Code, the following different situations shall be distinguished:
(1) Where the innocent party meeting the requirements of Article 1,091 of the Civil Code, as the plaintiff, files a claim for damages with the People's Court based on that article, it must be brought simultaneously with the divorce proceedings.
(2) In a divorce case where the innocent party meeting the requirements of Article 1,091 of the Civil Code is the defendant, if the defendant neither agrees to the divorce nor files a claim for damages based on that article, it may file a separate lawsuit on this matter.
(3) In a divorce case where the innocent party is the defendant, if the defendant fails to file a claim for damages under Article 1,091 of the Civil Code during the first instance but raises it during the second instance, the People's Court shall conduct mediation; if mediation fails, the parties shall be informed to file a separate lawsuit. If both parties agree to have the second instance People's Court handle the matter together, the second instance People's Court may render a joint judgment.

Article 89 After the parties have completed divorce registration procedures at the marriage registration authority, if a party files a claim for damages with the People's Court on the grounds of the provisions of Article 1,091 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall accept the case. However, if the party has explicitly waived such claim at the time of consensual divorce, the People's Court shall not support it.

Article 90 Where both spouses have fault circumstances as specified in Article 1,091 of the Civil Code, and one or both parties file a claim for divorce damages against the other, the People's Court shall not support it.
VI. Supplementary Provisions
Article 91 This Interpretation shall come into force as of January 1, 2021.
